name: llm-quant-a40

scenario.name: llm-quant-a40
scenario.description: Tasks 8.4 and 8.5 on one Runpod A40, dev split: what quantizing the planner's base and merging its adapter do to accuracy, latency under load and memory, and the self-hosted p95 under load that D7 needs. Base Qwen3.5-4B (8.3's, pinned) and its chosen adapter all-r4 (pinned by sha256, D42). Quantized bases (chosen 2026-10-24): RedHatAI's GPTQ checkpoints of the same base weights made with LLM Compressor, W4A16 (INT4 weights, the 4-bit rung the task names) and W8A8 (INT8 weights and activations, a second rung), pinned by revision; the vision tower, embeddings, lm_head and the linear-attention layers stay BF16, so only the full-attention and MLP projections are quantized (the same modules the adapter is on). The adapter, trained on the BF16 base, is served on each quantized base unchanged. Merged: all-r4 merged into the BF16 base on the pod (FP32 merge, BF16 weights; scripts/lora_merge.py) and served as a plain model, against the same adapter served by vLLM's LoRA path. One variable per comparison: base precision (same adapter, prompt, flags), adapter vs merged (same weights in effect, prompt, flags). Every server runs the deployment configuration of D40: prefix caching on, structured outputs on, greedy, thinking off. The base few-shot control runs the service's full prompt; the adapter and the merged model the compact prompt they were trained with. Each variant is load tested (closed loop, warmup excluded, 3 reps, concurrency up to 32 to find saturation) and records the dev split for the replayed eval (make eval-replay). Servers in priority order: a server that fails is recorded and the rest still run.

notes: Closed-loop load on the planner's real first-attempt prompts (dev questions), warmup excluded; times are measured on the pod (client and server on one host). valid_rate = first-attempt replies that parse and pass the planner's validation.
